statusDetail: Coverage-complete audit across six representative public surfaces. Purchase submission and authenticated account pages were intentionally not exercised.

page.framework: Amazon server-rendered MPA with extensive AUI client modules
page.notes: Italian marketplace rendered in English for the test location. Fresh profiles receive a large cookie consent dialog and AWS WAF challenge.

artifacts.caption: Heap summary after repeated menu interaction
Product page on a 360px device, scaled desktop layout

checkOutcomes.evidence: Under prefers-color-scheme: dark, computed body background remains rgb(255,255,255), root color-scheme remains normal, and the dark screenshot is visually unchanged.
The reduced-motion probe matched the reduce preference but still found three running leftToRight animations with 2000 ms duration.

checkOutcomes.method: Screenshot under prefers-contrast: more plus Lighthouse contrast audit
checkOutcomes.evidence: All controls and text remained visible; Lighthouse color-contrast scored 1.
The feature probe found only the browser root view-transition name and no authored transition names across homepage, product, cart, help, and sign-in surfaces.
The DOM probe found zero ScrollTimeline animations on the long homepage and product page.
Across probes, only the homepage exposed one scroll-snap container; product, cart and help exposed none, while no declarative gesture affordance was found.
The 4,376 px homepage and 9,003 px product screenshot show static chrome; probes found no scroll timelines or scroll-state behavior.
The DOM contains many role=dialog navigation flyouts but the computed-style probe found zero anchored elements and no popovers.

checkOutcomes.method: Focus and navigation probes plus screenshots
checkOutcomes.evidence: Skip links, descriptive navigation, persistent cart state, and strong orange/blue focus rings guide attention across pages.
Desktop and mobile load screenshots show a fixed consent panel covering the centre of the first viewport before interaction.
The consent surface is a FORM role=dialog; axe reports that dialog is not allowed on that element. The site has no dialog, popover, or details elements.
The full homepage screenshot is 4,376 px tall and gives substantial space to two navigation rows, repetitive promotional tiles, and a multi-column footer.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct evidence from evidence/home-mobile-layout.json, evidence/home-mobile.png, evidence/product-mobile.png
checkOutcomes.evidence: At 360x800 the homepage layout primitive reports no viewport meta, a 1000 px layout viewport, and 640 px overflow. The product page is scaled to 0.36, making text tiny.
Homepage exposed 23 container-query containers and product/cart/help each exposed a component container.
Lighthouse fails target-size with two affected groups; the mobile screenshot also shows dense header and card controls.
Search, product Add to basket, cart checkout, sign-in Continue, and help search each present an obvious next action.
Search results link to products with visible price and Add to basket; cart exposes checkout and sign-in continuity. No purchase was placed.

checkOutcomes.method: Empty-cart, help, and fallback state inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: The empty cart offers deals/sign-in, help offers task-based recovery, and malformed direct auth routes show a clear Home recovery link.
Lighthouse reports FCP 6.9 s and LCP 16.3 s, with performance score 0.58. The separate desktop trace still records LCP 4.09 s.
Desktop and mobile layout observers recorded CLS 0; Lighthouse also reports CLS 0.
Trace recorded no long tasks and 0 ms TBT; Lighthouse reports 110 ms TBT, within a good range.
HAR summary records 2.43 MB over 99 requests, 21 fonts using 729 KB, ten render-blocking candidates, and a 591 KB WAF script that took 3.02 s.
Lighthouse estimates 661 KiB unused JavaScript and 190 KiB unused CSS across the tested load.
axe reports critical aria-allowed-attr failures on search controls, an invalid dialog role on the consent form, and a select labeled only by title. Lighthouse also fails ARIA audits.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse contrast audit and high-contrast screenshot
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse color-contrast scored 1 and the prefers-contrast screenshot retained visible text and controls.
The homepage has no h1, begins visible content at h3/h4, and axe reports heading-order and region violations.
The product mobile screenshot shows a 1000 px desktop layout scaled to 0.36 on a 360 px device because the viewport meta tag is absent.
Both mobile layout captures lack viewport metadata; Lighthouse fails target-size and the homepage reports 640 px horizontal overflow.
Lighthouse fails errors-in-console and records one console error item.
The images primitive finds 38 of 39 images missing dimensions; Lighthouse identifies six incorrect-aspect-ratio images.
Lighthouse reports one deprecation warning on the homepage.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM metadata inspection on homepage and product
checkOutcomes.evidence: Homepage and product have unique descriptive titles and meta descriptions; cart/help/auth utility pages have descriptive titles.
Lighthouse fails crawlable-anchors; probes show javascript:void(0) navigation links, and mobile evidence confirms no viewport meta.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct evidence from evidence/home-probe.json, evidence/product-probe.json, evidence/sitemap.xml.headers
checkOutcomes.evidence: Homepage and product canonical URLs exist and robots.txt returns 200, but probes expose no hreflang links and /sitemap.xml returns 404.
The product probe found no JSON-LD and no Open Graph tags despite visible product name, price, availability, ratings, and imagery.

Headers evidence reports no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame protection, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy. Cookie evidence finds four cookies without Secure and auth-like session cookies without HttpOnly.
Tracker evidence sees 10 third-party origins and the HAR attributes 90 requests and 2.10 MB to origins other than www.amazon.it, including advertising and session telemetry endpoints.

checkOutcomes.method: Auth DOM/script inspection and load observation
checkOutcomes.evidence: No permission prompt appeared on load; the sign-in page loads IdentityWebAuthnAssets and presents a passkey error state in its DOM.
The main document has no clickjacking policy, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, CSP, or HSTS according to the headers primitive.
Discoverability fetch received HTTP 202 with only 2,007 bytes; just 1% of rendered content tokens were present and the primitive classified the response as a JS shell.

checkOutcomes.method: Representative overlay, cart, product, and help inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: The tested menus, consent controls, cart state, product details, and help page rendered without clipped active content or blank application shells.
Amazon commerce requires live inventory, price, account, and payment services; an offline checkout or installable app was not treated as a requirement.
checkOutcomes.reason: Amazon commerce requires live inventory, price, account, and payment services; an offline checkout or installable app was not treated as a requirement.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Malformed direct sign-in paths render a concise recovery page with a Home link instead of a blank shell; cart and help provide actionable empty/recovery states.
The English Italian-market page sets lang=en-gb, but dir is absent, hreflang is absent, and the style probe counts 658 rules using physical left/right properties.
English content consistently uses euro currency and localized commercial labels on the Italian market surface.
No event time, schedule, recurring interval, or time-zone-sensitive task appears in the audited shopping, cart, sign-in, or help surfaces.
checkOutcomes.reason: No event time, schedule, recurring interval, or time-zone-sensitive task appears in the audited shopping, cart, sign-in, or help surfaces.

checkOutcomes.method: Consent, product, cart, sign-in, and help screenshot review
checkOutcomes.evidence: Consent offers Accept and Decline side by side; pricing, basket actions, sign-in terms, returns, and cancellation help links are plainly disclosed.

checkOutcomes.method: Sign-in form semantics and recovery inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: The sign-in field is an email control with a visible label and the account flow provides Need help; recovery pages provide a direct Home action.
The sign-in identity field uses autocomplete=username and an email input type; search and help controls have explicit labels.

checkOutcomes.method: Product, cart, sign-in, and help flow review
checkOutcomes.evidence: Prices and Add to basket are visible before commitment; checkout is separated; account terms and Help are visible; cancellation and returns links are discoverable in help.
The image primitive finds 37 legacy-format images, 29 without srcset, 24 below-fold images not lazy loaded, and 38 without both dimensions.
Trace found no long tasks and no autoplay media; the page has no video and no known third-party tracker match, despite the separately reported transfer budget issue.
HAR records 729 KB across 21 fonts and 2.10 MB across non-main origins; the WAF challenge alone is 591 KB.
Product and homepage probes found no agent tool registration or structured action interface; product JSON-LD is also absent, leaving agents to infer controls from a large DOM.
No summarisation or generative task in the audited commerce flow requires on-device inference.
checkOutcomes.reason: No summarisation or generative task in the audited commerce flow requires on-device inference.

checkOutcomes.method: Thirty repeated hamburger open/close cycles with heap sampling
checkOutcomes.evidence: Heap samples were 21.96 MB, 24.66 MB, 16.90 MB, and 19.03 MB across three batches, showing collection rather than monotonic retained growth; DOM nodes stayed at 2,009.
Baseline snapshot was 32.48 MB self size and runtime used heap about 22 MB, proportionate to the large commerce page though optimization remains desirable.

checkOutcomes.method: Before/after heap summaries and repeated interaction DOM counts
checkOutcomes.evidence: DOM count remained 2,009 through 30 cycles; no Detached constructor appeared in either top-constructor summary and heap fell after collection.

paths.description: Homepage and global shell, representing navigation, promotions, consent, preferences, performance, security, and mobile behavior.
Search results for cuffie, representing the primary product-discovery listing and search journey.
Representative product detail and add-to-basket entry, covering price, product content, recommendations, metadata, and mobile detail layout.
Basket and checkout entry, representing empty state, account continuity, and commercial commitment.
Sign-in surface reached from the homepage OpenID link, representing account input, autocomplete, passkey assets, terms, and recovery.
Customer service gateway, representing task recovery, returns, cancellation, and support navigation.

findings.summary: The site does not follow the user’s dark colour preference.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-color-scheme: dark, computed body background remains rgb(255,255,255), root color-scheme remains normal, and the dark screenshot is visually unchanged.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare light and dark support early, set color-scheme on :root, and retint surfaces using prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Animations continue when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe matched the reduce preference but still found three running leftToRight animations with 2000 ms duration.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable non-essential animations in a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce query and remove auto-advance motion.

findings.summary: Page and state changes do not expose meaningful View Transition treatment.
findings.evidence: The feature probe found only the browser root view-transition name and no authored transition names across homepage, product, cart, help, and sign-in surfaces.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document or cross-document View Transitions for route and major state changes, with reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Scroll-related presentation does not use declarative scroll timelines.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found zero ScrollTimeline animations on the long homepage and product page.
findings.suggestedFix: Where scroll-linked effects are useful, use CSS animation-timeline instead of main-thread scroll handlers.

findings.summary: Long product and listing surfaces offer little platform-native gesture support.
findings.evidence: Across probes, only the homepage exposed one scroll-snap container; product, cart and help exposed none, while no declarative gesture affordance was found.
findings.suggestedFix: Use scroll snap and overscroll behavior for relevant carousels and gesture surfaces, while preserving native scrolling.

findings.summary: Navigation chrome does not react to the user’s position on very long pages.
findings.evidence: The 4,376 px homepage and 9,003 px product screenshot show static chrome; probes found no scroll timelines or scroll-state behavior.
findings.suggestedFix: Use scroll-state container queries or a lightweight progress affordance on long detail and listing pages.

findings.summary: Flyouts and menus use custom positioning rather than resilient CSS anchoring.
findings.evidence: The DOM contains many role=dialog navigation flyouts but the computed-style probe found zero anchored elements and no popovers.
findings.suggestedFix: Migrate transient flyouts to popover plus CSS anchor positioning with position-try fallbacks.

findings.summary: A large cookie consent panel obscures the primary content on every fresh visit.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile load screenshots show a fixed consent panel covering the centre of the first viewport before interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, non-obscuring consent surface where legally permitted, keep equally prominent accept and decline actions, and remember the decision.

findings.summary: The consent modal and navigation overlays are custom ARIA widgets rather than native primitives.
findings.evidence: The consent surface is a FORM role=dialog; axe reports that dialog is not allowed on that element. The site has no dialog, popover, or details elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog for modal consent and popover for transient navigation, with native focus and dismissal behavior.

findings.summary: Dense navigation, repeated cards, and a very large footer compete with shopping content.
findings.evidence: The full homepage screenshot is 4,376 px tall and gives substantial space to two navigation rows, repetitive promotional tiles, and a multi-column footer.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce duplicate promotional modules and collapse secondary navigation and footer chrome behind clear disclosure controls.

findings.summary: Pages omit the viewport meta tag and render as a desktop canvas on phones.
findings.evidence: At 360x800 the homepage layout primitive reports no viewport meta, a 1000 px layout viewport, and 640 px overflow. The product page is scaled to 0.36, making text tiny.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width=device-width, initial-scale=1 and replace fixed desktop assumptions with intrinsic, fluid layout.

findings.summary: Several controls and links are too small or too tightly spaced for touch.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails target-size with two affected groups; the mobile screenshot also shows dense header and card controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide at least 24 by 24 CSS px targets with adequate spacing, preferably larger for primary controls, while preserving visible focus.

findings.summary: The homepage is slow to become useful on the Lighthouse mobile profile.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports FCP 6.9 s and LCP 16.3 s, with performance score 0.58. The separate desktop trace still records LCP 4.09 s.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP content, reduce WAF and critical-chain cost, preload only the actual LCP asset, and defer non-critical modules.

findings.summary: Critical delivery is heavy and contains long blocking chains.
findings.evidence: HAR summary records 2.43 MB over 99 requests, 21 fonts using 729 KB, ten render-blocking candidates, and a 591 KB WAF script that took 3.02 s.
findings.suggestedFix: Shorten the critical chain, subset and consolidate fonts, cache static resources, and keep bot defense off the rendering path where possible.

findings.summary: The homepage ships substantial code that Lighthouse does not use.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 661 KiB unused JavaScript and 190 KiB unused CSS across the tested load.
findings.suggestedFix: Split page-specific bundles, conditionally load secondary features, and remove duplicate or legacy modules.

findings.summary: Critical controls contain invalid ARIA and incomplete visible labeling.
findings.evidence: axe reports critical aria-allowed-attr failures on search controls, an invalid dialog role on the consent form, and a select labeled only by title. Lighthouse also fails ARIA audits.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native semantics first, remove unsupported ARIA attributes, and give every control a persistent visible label.

findings.summary: Heading and landmark structure is inconsistent.
findings.evidence: The homepage has no h1, begins visible content at h3/h4, and axe reports heading-order and region violations.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide one clear page h1, preserve a logical heading hierarchy, and contain page sections within named landmarks.

findings.summary: Mobile text is rendered at desktop scale and becomes difficult to read.
findings.evidence: The product mobile screenshot shows a 1000 px desktop layout scaled to 0.36 on a 360 px device because the viewport meta tag is absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a real mobile viewport, fluid typography, comfortable line lengths, and reflowing product columns.

findings.summary: The page fails mobile reflow and touch-target expectations.
findings.evidence: Both mobile layout captures lack viewport metadata; Lighthouse fails target-size and the homepage reports 640 px horizontal overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow user scaling, add a correct viewport declaration, reflow to 320 CSS px, and enlarge small targets.

findings.summary: The homepage logs a browser error during load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails errors-in-console and records one console error item.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve the logged network or runtime error and add regression monitoring for uncaught errors.

findings.summary: Numerous images lack stable dimensions and some render at the wrong aspect ratio.
findings.evidence: The images primitive finds 38 of 39 images missing dimensions; Lighthouse identifies six incorrect-aspect-ratio images.
findings.suggestedFix: Set intrinsic width and height or aspect-ratio for images, and ensure transformations preserve the source ratio.

findings.summary: A deprecated browser API is still used.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports one deprecation warning on the homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the deprecated API with its current platform equivalent and test against the Baseline support target.

findings.summary: Some navigation links are not crawlable and the page is not mobile friendly.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails crawlable-anchors; probes show javascript:void(0) navigation links, and mobile evidence confirms no viewport meta.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real href destinations for navigation and add a standards-compliant viewport declaration.

findings.summary: Localized indexing signals are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Homepage and product canonical URLs exist and robots.txt returns 200, but probes expose no hreflang links and /sitemap.xml returns 404.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish consistent hreflang alternates for language variants and advertise the correct sitemap index from robots.txt.

findings.summary: The product page lacks structured product and social-preview metadata.
findings.evidence: The product probe found no JSON-LD and no Open Graph tags despite visible product name, price, availability, ratings, and imagery.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate schema.org Product and Offer JSON-LD plus Open Graph metadata matching the visible product.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS, but baseline security headers and cookie flags are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence reports no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame protection, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy. Cookie evidence finds four cookies without Secure and auth-like session cookies without HttpOnly.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy CSP and HSTS, add nosniff and frame protection, and apply Secure, HttpOnly, and appropriate SameSite attributes to cookies.

findings.summary: The initial page load has a broad telemetry and cross-origin footprint.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence sees 10 third-party origins and the HAR attributes 90 requests and 2.10 MB to origins other than www.amazon.it, including advertising and session telemetry endpoints.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimise initial telemetry, defer optional analytics until consent, batch events, and treat related Amazon domains as explicit privacy boundaries.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are absent.
findings.evidence: The main document has no clickjacking policy, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, CSP, or HSTS according to the headers primitive.
findings.suggestedFix: Set frame-ancestors, a strict referrer policy, a least-privilege permissions policy, HSTS, and a nonce or hash based CSP.

findings.summary: Core content is effectively unavailable to a generic non-JavaScript crawler.
findings.evidence: Discoverability fetch received HTTP 202 with only 2,007 bytes; just 1% of rendered content tokens were present and the primitive classified the response as a JS shell.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve meaningful HTML for core navigation and commerce content, and ensure bot protection does not replace it for legitimate non-JS clients.

findings.summary: Localized pages rely heavily on physical CSS and do not publish direction metadata.
findings.evidence: The English Italian-market page sets lang=en-gb, but dir is absent, hreflang is absent, and the style probe counts 658 rules using physical left/right properties.
findings.suggestedFix: Set explicit language and direction, publish language alternates, and migrate layout to logical inline and block properties.

findings.summary: Image delivery misses several basic efficiency controls.
findings.evidence: The image primitive finds 37 legacy-format images, 29 without srcset, 24 below-fold images not lazy loaded, and 38 without both dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Use responsive srcset and sizes, modern formats where supported, lazy-load below-fold images, and retain explicit dimensions.

findings.summary: Fonts, WAF, and third-party scripts consume a disproportionate initial-load budget.
findings.evidence: HAR records 729 KB across 21 fonts and 2.10 MB across non-main origins; the WAF challenge alone is 591 KB.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a purpose-based page-weight budget, subset fonts, consolidate families, and defer non-essential third-party code.

findings.summary: The commerce experience exposes no structured agent action surface.
findings.evidence: Product and homepage probes found no agent tool registration or structured action interface; product JSON-LD is also absent, leaving agents to infer controls from a large DOM.
findings.suggestedFix: Treat this as an emerging opportunity: expose safe, scoped commerce tools or agentic forms with explicit confirmation for consequential actions.

taskList.title: Restore a true responsive mobile layout
Move bot defense and heavy delivery work off the critical path
Deploy baseline security headers and secure cookie flags
Repair ARIA, labels, headings, and landmarks
Serve meaningful core HTML to non-JavaScript clients
Make consent less obstructive while preserving equal choice
Optimize responsive image and font delivery
Publish product structured data and localized indexing signals
Modernize navigation motion, anchoring, and scroll state
Reduce repetitive chrome and physical-direction CSS
Explore safe structured commerce tools for agents
Remove console errors and deprecated API use
